notes: The app can no longer fail to load because of a storage hiccup. A crash during playback is Android killing the page (the music lives in a WebView), and a page killed mid-write leaves the phone’s database needing recovery — so the boot right after it met a first storage read that FAILED, and the app drew “Add some music to get started” over a library that was still there. A failed read is no longer mistaken for an empty library: the library is read again through a fresh connection, and if that still cannot read it the app says so — “Your songs are still on this phone, nothing has been deleted” — with a Try again button, instead of an empty screen

One failed read no longer breaks every later one. The database handle was cached along with its failure, so a single transient error poisoned the whole session: every read after it returned nothing and nothing could be saved again until the app was closed and reopened. A failure is never remembered as final now, and the next read simply reopens

A wedged database can no longer freeze the app. Opening storage had no timeout and no handling for another connection holding it, so in the worst case the library never loaded at all and the app sat there — that is the “it just won’t load after it crashes” half of the report. An open now has a deadline, is retried once through a fresh connection, and a real failure takes over the screen with an explanation rather than a spinner

The on-device backup restore no longer runs on a guess. It treated a failed meta read as a wiped store, which meant a storage hiccup could rewrite playlists, albums and settings from an older backup and then reload — all on top of a library that was never missing. It now refuses to restore unless it can prove the stores are really empty

Fewer native calls while you play: the lock-screen controls are re-asserted when the session can actually have been rebuilt (coming back to the app, the player being released and re-armed, or the player arming) rather than on every single song start, which was handing the phone a fresh callback for all eight buttons per track
Saves that fail while storage is busy are logged instead of being left as rejected promises nothing owns
